warnings.why: A private health spending share of 2.02 percent is extremely low and implausible even for nations with heavily public-funded or donor-dependent health systems, as out-of-pocket and private employer spending typically form a higher baseline.

A private share of 3.22 percent is unrealistically low for a developing nation where informal out-of-pocket payments for medicines and care usually comprise a significantly larger portion of total health expenditure.
